The orchestrator — coordinating agent fleets from one kolu terminal

Reference·budding·implemented·JUL 16, 2026

The coordinator model behind kolu's multi-agent campaigns — one supervising session dispatching implementing agents into kolu terminals, with briefs+goals, file-based asks, lens-run gates, venue arbitration, and a live dashboard. The /orchestrator skill is the law; this note is the map.

Contents

  • The shape
  • The gates
  • Resources and truth
  • Why a terminal fleet at all

Kolu’s larger campaigns (the SR surface consolidation, the flake certification, the stdio-lifetime lineage, kolu-cli’s three faces) run on one model: a coordinator — an agent in its own kolu terminal — dispatches implementing agents into further kolu terminals, brokers their questions and gates, and owns the record, while the human sits one layer up and rules on forks. The operational rules live in the /orchestrator skill and evolve there (running memory, one lesson per recorded failure); this note records the architecture and why each piece exists, so the skill’s rules read as consequences rather than folklore.

The shape

One coordinator terminal; one worktree + terminal + branch per lane. Every dispatch is a brief file (scope, plan-of-record pointer, gates, laws, venue) plus a pinned /goal — the goal is the persistent artifact the harness re-surfaces, so anything that must survive a long context (the AskUserQuestion ban, “stop only on the coordinator’s stand-down”) rides the goal, not just the brief.Both learned from failures: an agent once stopped overnight mid-campaign while blocked (no goal pinned), and another opened a midnight question dialog at the human despite the ban being in its brief — briefs are read once and lose to long context. Agents never ask the human anything: every question is a file + one-line pointer to the coordinator’s terminal, blocking — and a blocking ask never idles a lane (the reply names what keeps moving). Goals carry the coordinator’s stand-down as their only stop condition — never a task metric, which cannot observe rulings.The certification goal “5 consecutive passes” kept re-firing its stop-hook after the campaign was honestly parked at 3/5 — the metric belongs in the brief’s done-criterion.

The gates

Anything design-bearing — a new symbol, signature, placement, or framework behavior — stops at a coordinator lens run before implementation: a workflow that grounds the design file’s claims (opus inventories, quoted file:line), judges them through the architecture lenses (fable), and adversarially refutes every real finding. The gate regularly changes designs for the betterRecorded outcomes: onEnd deleted as zero-caller machinery; a latent EPIPE exit-code bug caught before the new exit semantics codified it; a design’s timing narrative falsified while its conclusion survived (the fix got stronger). and occasionally the judgment falls to the coordinator directly (documented exception when infrastructure fails twice) — always on the record, cited in the PR body. Review depth is per-lane: full /be-review gauntlet by default; the human sometimes replaces it with dogfood (he uses the thing as the review) for UX-shaped work.

Resources and truth

CI venues are coordinator-arbitrated: darwin boxes are single-tenant and granted per dispatch (co-tenants like a foreign CI daemon make “quiet box” a verified claim, not an assumption); the coordinator’s own host is part of every lane’s transport path, so heavy local work waits until no lane flies. Class gates are re-derived from the current diff, never a PR’s original label. Evidence is exact-SHA; a red is reported before any rerun, and reruns are for errored (infra) only — never to wash a test signal. The coordinator verifies agents’ load-bearing claims independently before acting on them, and owns the shared records: the atlas branch (ambient, never a merge-queue nag), the flaky tracker, and the dashboard — a tracks tree (campaign rails with live lanes nested inside their active station), data in one git-untracked file, rendered by skill-versioned assets in the Code tab, with deep links making it a control surface.

Why a terminal fleet at all

The alternatives — everything in one context, or headless subagents — lose what the terminal fleet keeps: each lane is observable (the human can open any tile and watch), durable (survives the coordinator’s compaction; a lane can be revived warm days later), addressable (deep links, the dashboard, kaval-tui send), and independently paced (a gauntlet grinds while another lane waits on a human ruling). The kolu-cli plan’s MCP face exists to make this same loop structured: the skills go MCP-first with the CLI as fallback once kolu mcp ships.
